newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end higher on bank-led rebound.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end higher on bank-led rebound.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks staged a rebound on Wednesday after three days of losses, lifted mainly by the banking sector while other sectors remained subdued amid interest rate uncertainty and worries in the property market.

The Hang Seng Index closed on a gain of 62.13 points, or 0.51 percent, at 12,136.32. Over the previous three sessions, the index had lost 758.34 points. Turnover was HK$7.06 billion compared with HK$9.06 billion on Tuesday.
"There was some bargain-hunting but the activity was limited," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.

He said investors were awaiting further direction from Wall Street, where stocks suffered a sharp two-day selloff on fears of higher interest rates before the Dow industrials closed on a gain of 27.57 points at 6,611.05 on Tuesday.
"If we don't get any nasty shocks from Wall Street...the downside is probably limited," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
But he said the upside in the local market was also limited.
"The trouble with the market is who is going to buy it? It keeps coming off," said Osborn.
"People have been more interested in short-term performance -- selling and looking to put the money elsewhere in the world's emerging markets," he added.
He said the market was likely to be under some pressure until investors got a clearer picture of where U.S. interest rates were going.
"At the moment the market is still undecided and I suspect we are going to get a period of very high volatility before we get any real direction," Osborn said.
Shares in HSBC Holdings rose HK$2.50 to HK$177.50 and Hang Seng Bank Ltd gained HK$1.50 to HK$77.75.
Dao Heng Bank Group Ltd advanced HK$0.80 to HK$33.80 and Wing Hang Bank Ltd finished on a gain of HK$0.70 at HK$33.60.
But fears of government intervention in the Hong Kong property market kept a lid on gains in the property sector.
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd rose HK$0.50 to HK$64.25 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd gained HK$0.25 to HK$61.25, but Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd fell HK$0.75 to HK$77.75.
